_format: Original items. {1} marks the blank. Six options; the FIRST TWO are the correct pair. Options are shuffled when served.

items.text: The new manager's {1} style, in which she rarely spoke in meetings and answered questions with a word or two, puzzled employees used to her talkative predecessor.
items.clue: "Answered questions with a word or two" versus a "talkative predecessor."
items.explanation: She rarely spoke and answered with a word or two, so her style used few words: laconic and taciturn. Garrulous and loquacious are a synonym pair, but they describe the talkative predecessor, not her: a classic trap pair.

items.text: Though the evidence against him seemed {1}, a second look revealed that most of it was circumstantial.
items.explanation: "Though … seemed" sets up a contrast with evidence that turned out weak, so it first seemed beyond dispute: irrefutable or incontrovertible. Spurious and specious describe how it turned out, not how it first seemed; scant and anomalous don't create the contrast.

items.text: Rather than answering her critics point by point, the author chose simply to {1} them in a short, scathing reply that addressed none of their arguments.
items.clue: "A short, scathing reply that addressed none of their arguments."
items.explanation: A scathing reply that ignores the arguments mocks the critics: deride and ridicule. Placate and mollify form a synonym pair, but a scathing reply does the opposite of soothing. Corroborate and acknowledge don't fit a reply that addresses none of their points.

items.text: The documentary's tone is surprisingly {1}: it treats a grim subject without sentimentality and lets the facts speak for themselves.
items.explanation: A tone that avoids sentimentality and lets facts speak is restrained or understated. Maudlin and mawkish (overly sentimental) are the opposite pair. Strident and whimsical don't fit letting the facts speak for themselves.

items.text: Early reviewers praised the composer's {1} output, more than four hundred works in thirty years, while overlooking how uneven its quality was.
items.clue: "More than four hundred works in thirty years."
items.explanation: Four hundred works in thirty years is a huge output: prolific and fecund. Meager and sparse are a pair meaning the opposite. Meticulous clashes with "uneven quality," and derivative says nothing about how much she produced.

items.text: Far from being {1}, the senator's change of position was the product of months of careful study and consultation.
items.clue: "Far from being" versus "months of careful study."
items.explanation: "Far from being" calls for the opposite of careful study: capricious or whimsical (sudden and unreasoned). Deliberate and considered are a pair that describes what the decision actually was. Principled and overdue aren't opposites of careful study.

items.text: The company's {1} approach to safety, with inspections skipped and warnings ignored for years, made the eventual disaster seem almost inevitable.
items.explanation: Skipping inspections and ignoring warnings shows careless unconcern: cavalier or lackadaisical. Punctilious and scrupulous are a pair meaning the opposite. Innovative and litigious don't describe neglect.

items.text: Although she was {1} in private, the novelist became animated and talkative whenever she spoke about her work in public.
items.clue: "Although" contrasts private behavior with being "animated and talkative."
items.explanation: "Although" contrasts her private manner with being talkative in public, so in private she said little: reticent or reserved. Voluble and loquacious describe her public manner, so they are the trap pair. Irascible and pedantic don't contrast with talkativeness.

items.text: The policy was intended to {1} the housing shortage, but by encouraging speculation it actually made the problem worse.
items.clue: "Intended to … but … actually made the problem worse."
items.explanation: "But … actually made it worse" means the intent was the opposite, to ease the shortage: alleviate or mitigate. Exacerbate and aggravate describe what actually happened, the trap pair. Document and forecast aren't opposites of making it worse.

items.text: Her account of the expedition, though entertaining, is largely {1}: no other member of the party recalls the dramatic rescue she describes.
items.clue: "No other member of the party recalls" the rescue.
items.explanation: If no one else remembers the rescue, her account is of doubtful truth: apocryphal or fabricated. Corroborated and substantiated are the opposite pair. Verbose and harrowing aren't explained by the others' lack of memory.

items.text: The young lawyer's {1} questioning of the witness, which included several unsupported accusations, drew a sharp rebuke from the judge.
items.explanation: Making unsupported accusations is hasty and ill-considered: impetuous or rash. Circumspect and prudent are a pair meaning the opposite. Laudatory and inaudible questioning wouldn't involve accusations or draw a rebuke for them.

items.text: Despite his {1} reputation, the critic turned out to be generous with young writers, often spending hours helping them revise their manuscripts.
items.explanation: "Despite" sets his reputation against generosity, so his reputation was harsh: acerbic or caustic. Magnanimous and benevolent describe how he actually behaved, the trap pair. Obscure and prolific don't contrast with generosity.

items.text: The novel's plot is {1}; readers will recognize every twist from dozens of earlier thrillers.
items.clue: "Readers will recognize every twist from dozens of earlier thrillers."
items.explanation: Twists familiar from dozens of earlier thrillers make the plot overused: hackneyed or trite. Original and innovative are the opposite pair. A convoluted or implausible plot isn't explained by readers having seen it before.

items.text: Investors grew {1} after the company missed its earnings targets for the third straight quarter.
items.explanation: Repeated missed targets make investors cautious: wary or chary. Sanguine and buoyant are an optimistic pair that the bad news contradicts. Complacent and garrulous don't follow from missed targets.

items.text: The historian argues that the treaty, often celebrated as a diplomatic triumph, in fact merely {1} the conflict; war broke out within a decade, and its signatories had made no real effort to prevent it.
items.clue: "Merely," and war "broke out within a decade."
items.explanation: "Merely" plus war breaking out within a decade means the treaty only postponed the conflict: delayed or deferred. Resolved and settled are the celebrated view the historian rejects, and averted contradicts the war that followed. Chronicled makes no sense for a treaty.
